### 🟡 Changes recommended A moderate active finding shows the rollback test does not exercise the wall-clock seam, so it could pass despite a regression in the old clock coupling.
1 open issue - [Rollback control bypasses the patched wall-clock seam](https://github.com/hemsoft-dev/chief/pull/153#discussion_r4457131650) · New
What changed in this PR This pull request makes recovery-verification fixtures independent of the wall clock by using a deterministic synthetic timestamp source and adds coverage for backward clock movement. **Changes:** - Adds a fixed synthetic `stamp()` helper for recovery fixtures. - Patches fixture and probe timestamp generation within each test. - Adds a rollback regression for recovery verification. The rollback control does not currently exercise the wall-clock seam because the fixture and probe clocks are already replaced with fixed helpers. It could pass even if the original wall-clock coupling regressed. The test should drive those clocks through the patched `datetime` or add a separate old-fixture failing control. | File | Summary | | --- | --- | | `tests/​test_t3_recovery_verification.py` | Introduces deterministic timestamp fixtures, scoped patches, and the wall-clock rollback regression test. | This pull request requires changes.

This rollback control does not exercise the wall-clock seam: `setUp()` has already replaced `admission.stamp` with the fixed `stamp` at line 30, and `u.now_iso` with the same fixed helper at line 31. Consequently `FakeT3.end()`/`run()` and the probe never call `admission.datetime.now()`, so changing `wall_clock.now.return_value` cannot affect any timestamp and this test would still pass even if the old wall-clock coupling regressed. Run this case with the shared helper and probe clock driven by the patched `datetime` (or add a separate old-fixture RED control) so the backward step actually changes the observation.

Verified against exact head `e7ea04aa92612d58f36159ef5664db331ee366c1` with a targeted mutation control: the published regression passes; restoring only the shared fixture's old ambient `admission.stamp` after setup makes that SAME published regression fail with the exact unknown-reconciliation assertion. The mutant has one assertion failure, zero errors; current code passes. The probe remains on its current synthetic clock in both variants. Thus the test does detect a return to the old shared clock coupling, even though its intended fixed path does not consume the patched ambient clock. No source change or assertion weakening is needed. Complete commands/logs and mutation harness are retained in `parent-mutation-and-index-proof.json`, `parent-regression-current.log` and `parent-regression-mutant.log` under the private evidence directory already recorded in the PR. This proves the regression's sensitivity, not the historical CI trigger, which remains unestablished.
